outlook.statement: Optimistic view barring unforeseen circumstances; targeting improvements in productivity, quality, and value addition; focus on enhancing tea production with quality standards; fertilizer plant upgrading to GSSP to increase production by 30% and expand to Bihar, Assam; sugar mill expanding to 8000 TCD with increased ethanol capacity for improved profitability; comprehensive government package for tea industry rejuvenation expected.

The Indian tea market is growing by approx. 3% per annum, with the branded business constituting 75% of the overall market (by value). Rapid growth of digital platforms and e-commerce have revolutionized access of garden fresh teas to consumers directly.

Government is considering to advance ethanol blending targets beyond the current E20 program towards higher blends such as E25 and E85/E100 backed by a faster rollout of flex fuel vehicles. This when implemented will be good for long term future of the industry.

The Government of India has expressed its continued support for the indigenous SSP industry under 'Make in India' initiative. The Government increased subsidy by Rs.2142/- per tonne w.e.f 1st April,2025 and further Rs.741/- per tonne w.e.f 1st April,2026.

The Company expects to earn sufficient taxable profit in future years, based on profitability projections after considering enhanced operational performance in view of ongoing expansion at certain units, to utilize carried forward unused tax losses within the time frame allowed under the Act.

The Management will continue to track and evaluate the impact of the rules notified by the Central/State Government post March 31, 2026 and consider the appropriate accounting effect in the relevant period, as needed.

The Govt. of Bihar had notified the Molasses Storage Licence Fee vide resolution dated 12-03-2010 published in Bihar Gazette extraordinary dated 12-03-2010 as Rupee 1 per quintal of Molasses produced whereas the licence Fee previously was paid at the flat rate of Rs 500 for a year. Aggrieved with the decision, the Company has challenged the notification dated 12-03-2010 in Hon'ble High Court Patna vide CWJC No. 4102 of 2011. After hearing, the Hon'ble Court has stayed the operation of Resolution dated 12-03-2010 till the pendency of the writ petition vide their order dated 27-04-2011. Accordingly, the difference of Rs 500 per year and Rupee 1 per quintal of total molasses produced is provided as liability for licence fee every year.
